about.title: Mountain View Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Mountain View sits between two of the Peninsula's busiest highways, and its collision numbers reflect that. In 2025, public records for the city show 422 injury collisions, with 565 people hurt and 2 lives lost. Collision counts run highest along US-101, El Camino Real, SR-85 and Shoreline Boulevard, and reports tend to cluster on Thursday evenings between 6 and 8 p.m., when many drivers are still on the road. If you were one of the people injured, the days that follow can feel like paperwork stacked on top of pain: adjuster calls, repair estimates, missed shifts, and a medical bill you did not plan for. LawProactive exists to make one part of that simpler. Tell us what happened, and we will connect you, free of charge, with an independent personal injury attorney who handles Mountain View car accident claims on contingency. We are not a law firm and we never bill you. Our only role is to shorten the distance between an injured person in Santa Clara County and someone qualified to look at the claim.

whyChoose.title: Why Mountain View Drivers Use LawProactive

items.title: California's clock is real, and it can be short
items.desc: Most car accident claims here must be filed within two years, but if a city truck, a county vehicle or a Caltrans-maintained stretch of US-101 or SR-85 is involved, a government claim may be due in as little as six months. An attorney can tell you which deadline applies to your crash.

items.title: Being partly at fault does not end your claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so a driver who was 20 percent responsible can still pursue the other 80 percent. The attorneys in our network know how insurers try to inflate your share and how to push back with evidence.

items.title: No fee unless there is a recovery
items.desc: Every attorney LawProactive connects you with works on contingency, and California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and lost enjoyment of life in ordinary car accident cases. Our connection service is free as well, so there is no upfront cost at any step.

items.question: The other driver's insurer keeps calling for a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are not required to give the other side's insurer a recorded statement, and most attorneys advise against it. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can later be used to shift fault onto you under California's comparative fault rules. Report the crash to your own carrier as your policy requires, and let an attorney handle communication with the other insurer.

items.question: I was hit on Shoreline Boulevard near the US-101 ramps. Does it matter that a Caltrans or City of Mountain View vehicle was involved?
items.answer: It matters a great deal. Claims against a public entity in California follow a different process, and the initial government claim often has to be filed within six months rather than two years. Because Mountain View streets, county roads and state highways are maintained by different agencies, sorting out which entity is responsible is something an attorney should look at early.

items.question: What should I save from the scene of a Mountain View crash?
items.answer: Keep photos of the vehicles, the roadway and any visible injuries, along with the police report number and the names of any witnesses. Hold on to medical records, receipts, and pay stubs showing missed work, and do not repair or dispose of your car until its condition has been documented. If nearby businesses along El Camino Real or Shoreline Boulevard have cameras, footage is often overwritten within days, so acting quickly helps.
